output.brief: The jump in write-offs is mostly a night-receiving problem at your own DC, not a Haverlow problem. After the night receiving team was cut from six to four on 27 July, chilled pallets received at night wait a median of about 3 h 52 min before reaching a chamber, up from 44 min. The staging lanes aren't refrigerated and run at 15–17°C overnight. Night write-off rates rose from 0.6% to 2.9%, for every supplier alike. Day shift is flat. Haverlow's trailer telematics show product at 2.4–3.5°C when the doors open, and the chambers held temperature. The high "receipt" probe readings are taken at receipt confirmation, after the long wait on the dock, so they measure DC delay, not supplier condition. Don't raise the chargeback or move volume. Restore the night team, or otherwise cap dock-to-chamber time, and track it weekly from scan data. Keep the receiving probe. Separately, pull Corriebank's claim-level data to check how much of the credit rise is over-claiming. That is unproven; the credits are the smaller part of the rise. I'm fairly confident (about 80%) in the main finding. The one thing I'd still check is that write-offs fall once the dock times recover.
